Its selected neighbourhood must be precisely one of
$$N_S(w_\ell)=\{\ell\},$$
or
$$N_S(w_\ell)=\{\ell,i\},
\qquad i\in I,$$
where  $I$  denotes the selected isolates.Indeed, in the second case, after deleting  $\ell$ , the only remaining selected neighbour is  $i$ , which must be inactive. Bipartiteness ensures that  $i$  cannot be adjacent to  $\ell$ , and therefore it has no selected neighbour.Centre deletion. Let  $c$  be a selected star centre. Deleting  $c$  leaves  $c$  itself formed by two of its leaves. Therefore minimality gives a different outside vertex  $w_c$  that becomes unformed.Its selected neighbourhood must be one of
$$N_S(w_c)=\{c\},
\qquad
N_S(w_c)=\{c,i\},\quad i\in I,$$
or
$$N_S(w_c)=\{\ell\},
\qquad N_S(\ell)=\{c\}.$$
The last case is exactly a private clean leaf witness, not a new type of witness.Consequently, if a centre has no private clean leaf witness, it necessarily has a direct deletion witness of the first two types.This establishes the proposed classification of the  $p$  and  $q$  centres.Distinctness. Every chosen witness has exactly one active owner in  $S$ :a leaf for a leaf witness;a centre for a direct centre witness.Its other possible selected neighbour is an isolate, which is inactive.Thus witnesses with different owners cannot coincide. In particular, the  $e$  leaf witnesses and  $q$  direct centre witnesses are all distinct.This is the crucial justification for counting  $e+q$  witnesses simultaneously.2. The incidence and resource counts are correctWrite
$$p=c-q,\qquad e=2c+s.$$
For each selected isolate  $i$ , let  $h(i)$  count its incidences with the chosen witness family  $W$ .The number of incidences is bounded by
$$\sum_i h(i)\le e+q-p
=c+s+2q,$$
because the  $p$  designated clean witnesses have no isolate helper.With  $a,b_2,b_3$  as defined in the question,
$$a+2b_2+3b_3\le c+s+2q.$$
Also,
$$n\ge c+2e+q+t
=5c+2s+q+t.$$
These counts are disjoint: centres, leaves, outside witnesses and touched selected isolates belong to four disjoint vertex classes.The accepted leaf-retaining theorem applies to the  $e$  leaf witnesses alone. If  $t_{\rm leaf}$  is the number of distinct isolates touched by those witnesses, then
$$2d\le 2c-e+t_{\rm leaf}
\le 2c-e+t.$$
Therefore
$$t\ge 2d+s.$$
Substituting  $t=a+b_2+b_3$  gives
$$\boxed{c+2q-b_2-2b_3\ge 2d.}\tag{B}$$

Its exact matching formulation and the distinct-helper accounting are in the supplied established theorem. established-witness-theorems.txt3. The simultaneous matching repair worksThis is the most important new part.Construct  $\Gamma$  with:left vertices: selected star centres;right vertices: selected isolates with  $h(i)=2$ ;one edge  $c-i$  for every leaf  $\ell$  of  $c$  whose chosen witness has helper  $i$ .Parallel edges are retained.3.1 Degree boundsInitially, a centre may have more than two incident edges in  $\Gamma$ .Now retain exactly two leaves at every centre, discarding exactly
$$e-2c=s$$
leaves.Restrict  $\Gamma$  to the incidences of the retained leaves.Every centre now has degree at most two.Every helper has degree at most two because it has exactly two incidences with the entire witness family  $W$ .Thus the restricted bipartite multigraph has maximum degree at most two.3.2 Edge budgetThere are exactly  $2b_2$  incidences at the  $h=2$  helpers.At most  $q$  of them can come from direct centre witnesses, since there are only  $q$  such witnesses and each has at most one helper.Hence the number of leaf incidences is at least
$$2b_2-q.$$

$$2b_2-q-s$$
edges.3.3 Matching lower boundEvery finite bipartite multigraph of maximum degree at most two is a disjoint union of paths, even cycles and isolated vertices.For every path or even cycle, a matching covers at least half its edges. A pair of parallel edges is a two-edge even cycle and satisfies the same statement.Therefore its maximum matching has size at least half its edge count.Writing  $\mu=\nu(\Gamma)$ , we obtain
$$2\mu\ge 2b_2-q-s.$$
Equivalently,
$$\boxed{q+s+2\mu-2b_2\ge0.}\tag{D}$$
This argument is valid for multigraphs, including parallel incidences. No finite enumeration is involved.3.4 Why the swaps are simultaneously compatibleThis deserves particular attention.Start with
$$E_A=(T\cap A)\cup
\big((R_0\cap B)\setminus I_{\ge2}\big),$$
where  $I_{\ge2}$  denotes the selected isolates with  $h\ge2$ .For every matched pair  $(c,i)$ , where  $c\in A$  and  $i\in B$ , let  $\ell$  be the leaf corresponding to its matching edge and  $w_\ell$  its chosen witness.Perform
$$E_A\longmapsto
(E_A\setminus\{w_\ell\})\cup\{\ell,i\}.$$
The resulting set remains a dissociation set:1. Centre:  $c$  is retained. It had no selected leaf in  $E_A$ , and now has precisely the newly added leaf  $\ell$  as its selected neighbour.2. New leaf:  $\ell$  has its centre  $c$  and its own chosen witness as its only possible neighbours in the retained universe. The witness  $w_\ell$  has been removed. Thus  $\ell$  sees only  $c$ .3. Helper:  $i$  had exactly two chosen witness neighbours. One,  $w_\ell$ , has been removed; the other remains. Thus  $i$  has degree exactly one in the new induced graph.4. Other helpers: A witness can have at most one isolate helper. Consequently, removing  $w_\ell$  cannot accidentally remove a residual witness belonging to a different matched helper.5. Matching disjointness: No two swaps use the same centre or helper. Therefore the new leaves and helpers are distinct.6. Witness conflicts: Edges between outside witnesses do not cause a problem. All retained witnesses lie in  $A$ , so edges between witnesses in opposite bipartition classes cannot have both endpoints retained. The newly added vertices lie in  $B$ .7. Selected edges: The selected edge components remain untouched. No chosen witness has a selected neighbour in those components.This proves simultaneous compatibility, rather than merely proving that each individual swap is valid.The reverse orientation gives the same construction for a matching between centres in  $B$  and helpers in  $A$ .Because  $\Gamma$  splits into these two colour classes, its maximum matching is the sum
$$\mu=\mu_A+\mu_B.$$
Averaging the two resulting dissociation sets gives
$$\begin{aligned}
\beta_2(G)
&\ge |S|-\frac{c-q+b_2+b_3-\mu}{2}.
\end{aligned}$$
Hence
$$\boxed{c-q+b_2+b_3-\mu\ge2d.}\tag{C}$$

$$7(B)+13(C)+3(D).$$

$$20c+4q+3s-b_3-7\mu\ge40d.$$
In particular, the  $b_2$  coefficient cancels exactly.From the resource estimate and  $t\ge2d+s$ ,
$$n\ge5c+3s+q+2d.$$
Therefore
$$\boxed{
4n\ge48d+9s+b_3+7\mu.
}$$
It follows that  $n\ge12d$ .The second combination is also correct:
$$\frac{10(B)+20(C)+5(D)}6.$$
It gives
$$5c+\frac56q+\frac56s-\frac53\mu\ge10d.$$
Multiplying by six,
$$30c+5q+5s-10\mu\ge60d.$$
Combining this with the resource estimate gives
$$\boxed{
6n\ge72d+q+13s+10\mu.
}$$
Thus both claimed certificates are valid.For  $d\le0$ , the desired assertion is immediate. For  $d>0$ , integrality gives
$$\boxed{|S|-\beta_2(G)\le\left\lfloor\frac n{12}\right\rfloor.}$$

$$n=12d>0.$$
The two stability inequalities imply
$$q=s=\mu=0,\qquad b_3=0.$$
Then (D) forces
$$b_2=0.$$
Since  $q=0$ , all  $c$  centres have a designated clean witness. Since  $b_2=b_3=0$ , every touched isolate has exactly one witness incidence.We have
$$t=a.$$
From (B),
$$c\ge2d.$$
On the other hand,
$$n\ge5c+2d$$
gives  $c\le2d$ . Hence
$$c=2d,\qquad t=a=c.$$
All remaining resource inequalities must be equalities. In particular:
$$e=2c,\qquad |S|=c+e+c=4c.$$
There are no selected edge components, no additional selected isolates, no unused outside vertices and no additional vertices outside the allocated witness system.The equality structure is therefore: $c$  selected copies of  $P_3$ ; $c$  selected isolates; $c$  private clean leaf witnesses; $c$  helper witnesses, each incident with a distinct selected isolate;no other vertices.Each helper isolate has exactly one neighbour in the entire graph, so it is pendant.Edges between outside witnesses are unrestricted except for bipartiteness and simplicity.This is a necessary equality structure, not a sufficient characterization of every possible interface.It agrees with the six-vertex-block construction in the supplied source, where the helper witnesses can be connected through arbitrary bipartite witness-to-witness edges. The construction with  $a=b=r$  gives
$$n=12r,\qquad |S|=8r,\qquad \beta_2(G)=7r.$$

Their total contribution is bounded by  $q$ ; after retaining two leaves per centre, the remaining helper-incidence graph has maximum degree two. $$\{c\}\quad\text{or}\quad\{c,i\},
\qquad i\in I.$$

$$a+2b_2+3b_3\le c+s+2q,$$
